title: Scalar and vector bosons in a Bonnor-Melvin-$Λ$ spacetime: an exact Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau analysis
authors: Francisco A. Cruz Neto, Luis B. Castro
abstract: We study scalar and vector bosons in the Bonnor--Melvin--$Λ$ spacetime within the Duffin--Kemmer--Petiau (DKP) formalism. By employing Umezawa's projection operators, we separate the physical spin-0 and spin-1 sectors and derive the corresponding exact second-order equations in the full curved spacetime, without relying on the conical approximation. For the scalar sector, the radial equation reduces to a Schrödinger-like equation with a trigonometric Pöschl--Teller effective potential. In the vector sector, the longitudinal mode is governed by the same effective potential, whereas the transverse polarizations are described by generalized trigonometric Pöschl--Teller potentials. Because the me\-tric function vanishes at a discrete set of radial points, the radial dynamics is naturally formulated as a singular Sturm--Liouville problem on a fundamental interval, with the physical radial domain fixed by the Friedrichs self-adjoint extension of the corresponding singular radial operators. As a result, all physical sectors exhibit purely discrete radial spectra, and their eigenfunctions are obtained in closed form. These results provide a unified exact treatment of scalar and vector bosons in the Bonnor--Melvin--$Λ$ spacetime, complement previous analyses based on the conical approximation, and clarify the role of the global geometric structure of the background in shaping confinement and spectral properties.
summary: This paper provides an exact quantum treatment of scalar and vector bosons moving in a specific curved spacetime (Bonnor-Melvin-$\Lambda$) using the Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau formalism. By rigorously analyzing the radial equations, the authors demonstrate that all physical modes possess purely discrete energy spectra. This work offers a significant improvement over previous approximations by incorporating the full global geometric structure of the background.
main_problem: To provide a unified, exact treatment of scalar and vector bosons propagating in the curved Bonnor-Melvin-$\Lambda$ spacetime background.
main_result: The analysis yields purely discrete radial spectra for all physical sectors (scalar, longitudinal, transverse) by solving singular Sturm-Liouville problems derived from the DKP formalism.
method: The authors use Umezawa's projection operators to reduce the Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau equation into separate second-order equations for spin-0 and spin-1 components, which are then solved using techniques leading to hypergeometric functions.
model_or_system: The system involves scalar ($\phi$) and vector ($W_\mu$) bosons propagating in a Bonnor-Melvin-$\Lambda$ spacetime. The dynamics are governed by the DKP formalism, yielding effective Klein-Gordon and Proca equations in curved spacetime.
key_observables: Purely discrete radial spectra (eigenvalues $\epsilon^2, \epsilon_s^2$) for all physical modes; conserved currents ($J_\mu$).
important_parameters: The cosmological constant ($\Lambda$); the background geometry parameters defining the metric function $S(r)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis avoids the conical approximation, working directly in the full curved spacetime. The radial dynamics are treated as a singular Sturm-Liouville problem on fundamental intervals.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the DKP formalism and projection operators for the given background. It then derives the second-order equations for the scalar and vector sectors, leading to radial equations that are solved by mapping them to known solvable forms (Pöschl-Teller/Hypergeometric). Finally, the quantization conditions yield the discrete spectra.
why_interesting: While not directly about AMO systems, the methodology of solving wave equations in curved backgrounds using exact spectral methods and identifying confinement mechanisms is highly relevant for quantum field theory in curved spacetime, which underpins many advanced topics in quantum optics and gravitational physics.
